title: serving-runtime weekly update - kernel, KV cache, batching (2026-06-03)
content:
Week ending 2026-06-03 - serving-runtime weekly sync (kernel optimizations, KV cache, batching)

Attendees: Priya, Evan, Lena, Marco, Aisha (notes below are a mix of updates + action items)

Highlights
- Kernel optimizations shipped to staging (PR #1284) — fused attention kernel and improved matmul tiling enabled. Initial staging benchmarks show ~14% throughput uplift for 8k-context workloads on A100.
- KV cache prefix caching prototype (ENG-4821) moved to integration tests; cache eviction policy updated to LRU-with-priority to reduce cold-call disk reads.
- Dynamic batch scheduler (PR #1291) improvements reduced p50 latency variance under bursty traffic. New scheduler is default on alpha nodes.

Kernel work (Priya, Evan, Marco)
- What shipped: fused attention + improved tiling heuristics landed in staging (1284). This includes a fallback path for legacy kernels to avoid regressions on uncommon shapes.
- Benchmarks (staging, redwood-7b, batch size distribution approximating production traffic):
  - baseline (pre-change): p50=48ms, p99=210ms, throughput=1200 tokens/sec/node
  - after fused kernels: p50=41ms, p99=170ms, throughput=1370 tokens/sec/node (+14%)
- Notes: p99 improved but still dominated by KV-cache misses and large prompt (>6k) slow paths. We saw a small regression for short-context (<64 tokens) cases in one micro-benchmark due to extra branching — added a fast-path flag to avoid this.
- Open work / blockers:
  - Kernel memory allocator: intermittent OOMs on some long-session traces. Likely due to slower free path in fused kernels. Action: Evan to instrument allocator free timings and open a follow-up PR (ENG-4890).
  - Need wider GPU compatibility tests (H100 / T4) before can flip rollout to prod. Marco to run nightly matrix tests (tracking ticket: ENG-4912).

KV cache (Lena, Aisha)
- Prefix caching prototype (ENG-4821) integrated into the cache service. Key changes: explicit prefix keys (prefix-hash + model-id), LRU-with-priority eviction, and async warm-up for predicted prefixes.
- Integration test results: when warm-up enabled, cache hit-rate on conversational workloads increased from 62% -> 78% for typical user flows (5-20 turn convos). Cold-start latency for first request still high — measured 280ms extra due to disk read + deserialize.
- Bugs found:
  - Memory leak: observed ~10MB/100k requests retained in descriptor map when evicting entries. Root cause appears to be stale reference in the metrics hook. Fixed locally; PR pending.
  - Consistency window: race between cache eviction and in-flight read causing occasional incorrect KV fetch. Mitigation implemented (lock striping + double-check) but needs load testing.
- Next steps:
  - Merge cache descriptor leak fix and run a 48h soak (Lena, ENG-4868).
  - Investigate moving cold storage to a faster serialized format (LZ4 vs snappy) — Aisha to prototype and report perf tradeoffs.

Batching & Scheduler (Marco, Priya)
- Dynamic batch scheduler changes (PR #1291) introduced per-model adaptive batch caps and idle-sla-aware flush thresholds. This reduces tail latency for low QPS models while preserving throughput for high QPS ones.
- Measured impact on alpha nodes (mixed workload):
  - Tail latency (99th) for low-QPS models: down 28%
  - Overall token throughput: neutral (+1% variance)
- Observed issues:
  - Under very bursty arrivals, scheduler occasionally creates many small batches leading to CPU sched overhead. Tunable parameter admitted: batch_coalesce_window_ms. We increased default from 3ms -> 6ms which reduced small-batch frequency.
  - Some models using large-key KV-cache combos still cause long serialization pauses; need to coordinate with KV team to rate-limit cache writes during large batch flushes.

Reliability / Incidents
- No customer-impacting incidents this week. Two internal test flakes: one OOM (kernel allocator) and one consistency race (KV cache). Both reproducible and being triaged.

Performance experiments in-flight
- Quantized-kernel compatibility matrix: running correctness + perf matrix against int8 variants for redwood-3b/7b. Early results: int8 gives 1.6x throughput but has a small increase in p99 for long-context workloads — likely due to extra dequant overhead on cache restore.
- KV cache async warm-up experiment: enabling warm-up for 20% of traffic reduces p99 by 12% at the cost of ~3% additional memory. Monitoring now for slow-rollout.

Action items (owner, due)
- Evan: add allocator free-time tracing + open ENG-4890 (due 2026-06-07).
- Marco: run GPU compatibility nightly matrix (H100/T4/A100) and upload reports (ENG-4912) (due 2026-06-09).
- Lena: merge descriptor-leak fix and start 48h soak on staging (ENG-4868) (due 2026-06-05).
- Aisha: prototype LZ4 serialization for cold-store and compare cold-read latencies vs snappy (deliverable: perf chart) (due 2026-06-10).
- Priya: schedule roll-forward canary (staging->canary) for fused kernels after allocator fix is in (target 2026-06-11).

Docs / PRs to review
- PR 1284 (kernel fused attention): need second approver on perf tests (requested Evan).
- PR 1291 (dynamic scheduler): please review config knobs and default values (requested Marco, Lena).
- Cache descriptor leak fix: draft PR linked in ENG-4868 (requested Lena/Aisha).

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: kernel allocator OOMs could cause prod regressions if rollout proceeds too quickly. Mitigation: hold canary until allocator tracing confirms stable free path; add rolling restart safeguards.
- Risk: KV cold-read latency impacting p99 for conversational customers. Mitigation: prototype faster serialization and async warm-up; consider ephemeral memory cache warmers on hot nodes.

Notes / random todos
- Add a short README for the new scheduler config keys in the console UI so SRE/Platform can tune without code changes.
- Consider exposing cache hit-rate per-customer in Optimize to diagnose regressed accounts faster.

Next meeting: weekly sync 2026-06-10 10:00 PT (agenda: allocator tracing results, KV soak report, canary plan)

End of notes.
